roles.name: Attorney for financial matters under an enduring power of attorney
roles.summary: An adult with capacity may appoint attorneys for financial matters in the approved form. The principal may say when financial power starts, including on impaired capacity. If nothing is stated, it starts when the document is made. It survives impaired capacity. Death revokes it. Later marriage or civil partnership revokes it except for the new spouse or partner. Divorce or ending a civil partnership revokes it as to the former spouse or partner.

assigned.event: Adult principal with capacity signs approved form before an eligible witness; attorney accepts by signing

starts.event: Time, circumstance or occasion stated in the document; if none stated, once made; if the principal loses capacity before a stated later start, during impaired capacity

ends.event: Death of principal
Principal later marries or enters a civil partnership (revoked except as to new spouse or civil partner, unless contrary intention)
Principal divorces or civil partnership is terminated (revoked as to former spouse or partner)
Written revocation by principal with capacity, or a later inconsistent enduring document
Attorney resigns, dies, loses capacity or becomes bankrupt (as to that attorney)
Supreme Court or QCAT removes attorney or revokes document

notes.text: Registration is optional (s 60). It matters for dealing with land, but it is not needed before the power can be used generally.
An individual attorney cannot have been a paid carer for the principal within the previous 3 years, and cannot be a health provider or a residential service provider for the principal.

roles.name: Attorney for personal (including health) matters under an enduring power of attorney
roles.summary: An enduring power of attorney may give power for personal matters, which include health matters. The principal cannot choose an earlier start: this power is exercisable only while the principal has impaired capacity for the matter. An advance health directive and any QCAT guardian rank ahead of the attorney for health matters.

roles.name: Attorney appointed by an advance health directive (and the directive itself)
roles.summary: In an advance health directive, an adult gives directions about future health care, which can include refusing life-sustaining measures. The adult may also appoint attorneys for health matters in case the directions prove inadequate. The document needs a doctor's or nurse practitioner's capacity certificate. Its directions and the attorney's power operate only while the principal has impaired capacity, and a direction takes priority over every other decision maker.

roles.summary: A general (non-enduring) power of attorney under Chapter 2. It is revoked by statute if the principal comes to have impaired capacity. Other revocation events, including the principal's death, are left to the general law.

roles.name: Statutory health attorney
roles.summary: If there is no applicable advance health directive, guardian or enduring attorney for a health matter, the statutory health attorney decides. This is the first readily available and culturally appropriate adult in this order: a spouse in a close and continuing relationship, then an unpaid carer, then a close friend or relation. If no one qualifies, the Public Guardian decides. The power exists only while the adult has impaired capacity for the matter.

starts.event: When the adult has impaired capacity for a health matter and no higher-priority decision maker applies

ends.event: Adult regains capacity
Higher-priority decision maker applies (advance health directive, guardian, enduring attorney)
Death of the adult (no express provision; power concerns health care of a living adult)

notes.text: If nobody listed is readily available and culturally appropriate, the Public Guardian is the statutory health attorney.

The statutory health attorney role comes from the Powers of Attorney Act 1998 (ss 62-63). Its priority against other decision makers is set by the Guardianship and Administration Act 2000 s 66, which prevails if the two Acts are inconsistent.

roles.name: Guardian appointed by QCAT
roles.summary: QCAT may appoint a guardian for personal matters, including health matters, if the adult has impaired capacity for the matter, a decision is needed or there is unreasonable risk, and the adult's needs or interests would not otherwise be met. The appointment ends automatically when the adult dies, among other events. QCAT reviews it at least every 5 years.

roles.name: Administrator appointed by QCAT
roles.summary: QCAT may appoint an administrator for financial matters on the same tests as a guardian. Since 30 November 2020 it may also appoint one for an adult who has been missing for at least 90 days. The appointment ends automatically on the adult's death, or on the administrator's bankruptcy. A missing-person appointment ends on a coroner's finding of death, a court declaration of death, or registration of the death.

roles.name: Executor (grant of probate)
roles.summary: At death, the deceased's property vests by statute in the executor named in the will. If there is no executor able and willing to act, it vests in the Public Trustee. On a Supreme Court grant, it vests in the grantee. A divorce, annulment, end of a civil partnership or end of a de facto relationship revokes the former partner's appointment as executor unless the will shows a contrary intention. Marriage revokes the whole will, with exceptions.

roles.name: Administrator (letters of administration) or Public Trustee administering under order or election
roles.summary: If there is no executor able and willing to act, property vests in the Public Trustee until the Supreme Court grants letters of administration. The Public Trustee may get an order to administer. For estates it estimates at $150,000 or less in Queensland, it may instead file an election, which has the same effect as an order.

notes.text: For small estates, if assets excluding land do not exceed $75,000, the Public Trustee may apply them to claims or pay those entitled without filing an election.

A person who takes estate property without a grant may be charged as an executor in their own wrong. Queensland has no general statutory protection for private holders who pay small sums without a grant, unlike Victoria's s 31A.

roles.name: Senior available next of kin (tissue donation)
roles.summary: Queensland uses opt-in consent. The deceased's own signed written consent, if not revoked, authorises removal. Otherwise a hospital designated officer may authorise removal if the senior available next of kin consents and reasonable inquiries show no objection by the deceased. The order is spouse, then adult child, then parent, then adult sibling. An objection by any one person of equal rank prevents removal. Since 2025 amendments, next of kin may also consent before death to ante-mortem interventions after a decision to withdraw life-sustaining measures.

ends.event: Decision made / tissue removed

notes.text: The deceased's own signed written consent, if not revoked, authorises removal by itself.
A parallel scheme applies when the body is not in a hospital (s 23).

roles.name: Personal representative / close relative controlling disposal of remains
roles.summary: At common law the executor, or the person entitled to administration, has the right to custody of the body for burial. The Cremations Act 2003 lets a close relative or personal representative apply for permission to cremate. It qualifies the common-law right in three ways. The personal representative must carry out signed cremation instructions. Otherwise an objection by a spouse, adult child, parent or personal representative blocks cremation. The crematorium must follow the applicant's reasonable written instructions for the ashes.

ends.event: Body buried, or cremated and ashes disposed of per applicant's instructions (or buried by crematorium after 1 year without instructions)

notes.text: Close relatives who may apply are a spouse, adult child, parent or adult sibling, or for an Aboriginal person or Torres Strait Islander, a person appropriate under tradition or custom. If none of these and no personal representative applies, another adult may apply with a satisfactory explanation.

poaDurableByDefault.note: A general power of attorney is revoked if the principal comes to have impaired capacity. Only an enduring power of attorney in the approved form survives.

springingPoaAllowed.note: For financial matters the principal may state any start time, circumstance or occasion; the default is on making. Personal and health matters are exercisable only during impaired capacity, and the principal cannot change that.

poaRegistrationBeforeUse.note: Registration is optional under s 60 and affects dealings with land. It is not a precondition to exercising power generally.

healthAgentStartsOn.note: Enduring attorneys for personal and health matters, advance health directive directions and statutory health attorneys all operate only while the adult has impaired capacity for the matter. No certificate is required to activate them.

supportedDecisionMakingStatute.name: None. There is no statutory supporter appointment. The Guardianship and Administration and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2019 (assented 11 April 2019; main parts commenced 30 November 2020) added general principles requiring support for decision-making, but not a supporter role.

digitalAssetsFiduciaryStatute.name: None found. The Succession Act 1981, Powers of Attorney Act 1998 and Guardianship and Administration Act 2000 (current reprints) contain no digital-asset or online-account access provisions.

onlineToolsRecognisedInLaw.note: No Queensland statute recognises platform online tools.

organDonationModel.name: Transplantation and Anatomy Act 1979 (Qld): deceased's signed consent or senior available next of kin consent absent objection

smallEstateWithoutGrant.note: No general statutory procedure lets family members or holders collect or pay a small estate without a grant. Only the Public Trustee may act without a grant: by filing an election for estates up to $150,000 (s 30), or by applying assets directly for estates up to $75,000 excluding land (s 35). Holders' own informal practices are not law.

probateGrantName.note: Supreme Court of Queensland grants probate, or letters of administration where there is no executor.

healthAgentPostDeathAuthority.note: Death revokes enduring documents, and QCAT appointments end automatically on death. After death, tissue donation goes to the senior available next of kin and disposal to the personal representative or close relatives.
